producer_report.summary: When a re-read ends as needs accepting, `run_job` now gives its `--job-limit` slot back. The `_ if run.needs_accepting` arm decrements `st.started` under the state lock. Root cause: the slot was taken before the read and never returned when the item was left queued, so `--job-limit 1` stopped the drain at `job limit` after an item that ran nothing. The JobLimit check, the increment and the passed, held and failed arms are untouched, and the re-read's cost still counts against the budget. I added `a_re_read_that_needs_accepting_does_not_use_a_job_limit_slot` to tests/drain.rs. I ran it with the decrement removed and it failed (landed 0, not 1: b never ran). With the decrement restored, all 162 tests in the drain binary pass. The module docs, the `Limits::max_jobs` doc, the `--job-limit` help, the `job limit` stop-reason text and a CHANGELOG entry all state the new rule.

With several workers, a worker that met the full limit while the needs-accepting item was in flight has already ended its own item with JobLimit; the returned slot does not undo that. The sequential case in the criterion is fixed. The code comment says so.
mistakes: My first version of the new test did not compile (`q.contains('a')` on an `Item`); I fixed it to `q.job == "a"` before any recorded run.
learnings: The Stub in tests/drain.rs returns a needs-accepting Run for any job named in `needs_accepting`; `report.queued` holds `Item` values with a `job` field, not strings.
The whole drain test binary takes about 130 seconds.
